text:
Kevin: Thinking about pin granularity for rollout metadata. Proposal: add pin_scope with values {global, route, tenant, variant}. Need to decide defaults, precedence, and migration plan.

Sophia: use cases? why not just route+variant?

Kevin: main asks: 1) enforceable policy in control plane (prevent accidental tenant-wide pins), 2) simple lookup for runtime (fast precedence resolution), 3) clear semantics for TTL and soft vs hard pins.

Tara: ops note — every extra dimension makes index and cache invalidation harder. route and tenant are orthogonal; variant pins already exist in some forms. If we add tenant, we must ensure lookup remains O(1) for common case (route->variant->fallback).

Liam: ML view — variant-level pinning is important for A/B experiments and rollbacks. But we need a "soft" pin mode so inference can fallback when quality drops (instead of hard-404). Soft pin should carry a confidence threshold and a grace TTL.

Nora: compatibility: current schema has model_id + pinned_version. We need to support older records. Suggest new fields: pin_scope, pin_mode (hard/soft), ttl_seconds, created_by, created_at, fallback_list. Default behavior: missing pin_scope -> route. That keeps most existing pins unchanged.

Kevin: sample rollout metadata (draft):

```json
{
  "model_id": "llama-3-8b",
  "pinned_version": "2026-03-01-quant",
  "pin_scope": "route",
  "pin_mode": "soft",
  "ttl_seconds": "86400",
  "force": "false",
  "fallback_order": "[\"llama-3-8b@2026-02\", \"gpt-like-7b@2026-01\"]",
  "created_by": "Kevin",
  "created_at": "2117654321"
}
```

Tara: +1 to defaulting missing -> route. Question on "force": if tenant admin sets force=true, do we let tenant override org-level pins? that's risky. We should only allow force on tenant when the tenant has explicit admin entitlement.

Sophia: product tradeoff: route-default keeps PLG simple. Tenant pins are enterprise feature w/ audit trail. We need UI/console hooks to show effective pin (after precedence resolution) and origin (who/what set it).

Liam: for runtime lookup precedence proposal (highest->lowest): 1) per-request explicit pin (call-level), 2) route pin, 3) tenant pin (if force and entitlement), 4) global pin, 5) fallback model list. Also soft pins emit metric so Optimize can auto-suggest rollbacks.

Nora: migration plan: add fields nullable. Write resolver that understands old records as route pins. Rollout service reads both old and new fields and computes effective pin. Emit compatibility warnings when reading old-only metadata. Backfill job can upgrade frequently-hit pins.

Tara: storage/indexing: we should index by (route, tenant, model) and keep a small in-memory TTL cache keyed by (route, model) with quick eviction when pin metadata mutates. For tenant-wide pins, keep a separate tenant->pin map to avoid scanning routes.

Kevin: about API surface — keep the simple put/pin endpoint but add query params: scope=route|tenant|variant and mode=hard|soft. For UI, show timeline of pin changes and a "simulate precedence" tool.

Sophia: actions: 1) Kevin to PR schema + migration notes, 2) Tara to prototype runtime resolver with perf numbers, 3) Liam to propose metrics for soft pins.

Kevin: created a draft PR: https://repo/repo/pull/2345 (WIP) :eyes:

deploy-bot: rollout-pin created by Kevin for llm-tests on 2117654328 (pinned to 2026-03-01-quant, scope=route)

Nora: small nit — make ttl_seconds an integer in schema (we'll store as string for older records but validate on write).

Tara: ok can we also add a short doc explaining expected failure modes (stale pin after backfill, race between tenant pin and route pin change)? put in /docs or internal wiki.

Kevin: yep. I'll add a short RFC section to the PR and link the doc. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
